ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: In the left diagram, the large balance has its right pan lower than its left pan. On the small balance sitting on the left large pan, W is on the left little pan and X is on the right little pan; the X side is lower. On the small balance sitting on the right large pan, Y is on the left little pan and Z is on the right little pan; the Z side is lower. In the right diagram, after two weights have been swapped, the large balance has its left pan lower. Also, on each of the two small balances in the right diagram, the left little pan is lower than the right little pan. Now reason from these tilts as inequalities. Initially, the image gives X > W, Z > Y, and Y + Z > W + X. In the final diagram, the left small balance must have left-position weight greater than right-position weight, the right small balance must also have left-position weight greater than right-position weight, and the total on the large left pan must exceed the total on the large right pan. Test the six possible swaps. WX would require Y > Z on the right small balance, contradicting Z > Y. WY gives final requirements Y > X and W > Z, which together with X > W and Z > Y creates an impossible cycle. XY would require W + Y > X + Z, but since X > W and Z > Y, actually X + Z > W + Y. XZ gives W > Z and Y > X, which contradicts the initial chain X > W and Z > Y. YZ would require W > X, contradicting X > W. For WZ, the final positions become Z versus X on the left small balance, requiring Z > X; and Y versus W on the right small balance, requiring Y > W; the large balance requires Z + X > Y + W. These are consistent with the initial inequalities, for example W = 1, Y = 2, X = 3, Z = 4. Therefore the swapped weights are W and Z.
